title: Analytics Rules, Anomalies and MITRE ATT&CK Coverage in Sentinel

header.html: 1. Manage a security operations environment (40 to 45%)

Configure and manage analytics rules in Microsoft Sentinel SIEM, including scheduled, near-real time (NRT), threat intelligence and machine learning; analyze attack vector coverage by using the MITRE ATT&CK matrix; configure anomalies in Microsoft Sentinel
the official Microsoft SC-200 study guide (skills measured as of October 21, 2026) and Microsoft Learn

toc.title: Threat intelligence and Microsoft security rules

html:
1Analytics rule types

Path: Microsoft Sentinel > Configuration > Analytics, with tabs Active rules, Rule templates and Anomalies. To use a template, select it and choose Create rule.

Rule type Purpose
Scheduled Runs a KQL query on a schedule; the most flexible
Near-real-time (NRT) Runs every minute, for fast detections on a single table
Threat intelligence (TI map) Matches indicators against your logs; template names start with TI map
Microsoft security Creates incidents from alerts of other Microsoft security products
Anomaly Machine learning models that flag unusual behavior; no alerts, results go to the Anomalies table
Machine learning behavior analytics Preview rules for SSH and RDP logons
Fusion One rule, on by default, with hidden logic that correlates multistage attacks

In the Defender portal, Fusion is disabled and Microsoft security (incident creation) rules are not available, because Defender XDR already creates those incidents.

Exam tip

. Scheduled = flexible. NRT = one minute, one table. Anomaly rules produce no alerts.

2Scheduled rules

The wizard has the steps General, Set rule logic, Incident settings, Automated response and Review + create.

Setting Detail
Query interval and lookback Each 5 minutes to 14 days
Start running Automatically, or At a specific time (preview; 10 minutes to 30 days after creation)
Ingestion delay Allow for a five-minute delay
Query length 1 to 10,000 characters; search * and union * are not allowed
Alert threshold Per run: minimum, maximum or exact number of results
Event grouping One alert per run (default), or one alert per event (up to 150 alerts, the last one summarizing the rest)
Suppression Stop running the rule for up to 24 hours after an alert
Results simulation Test against the last 50 runs
Severity Informational, Low, Medium, High
Rule logic concept Why it matters
Entity mapping Maps columns to entities (account, host, IP); required for the investigation graph
Custom details and alert details Show extra fields and dynamic titles in the alert
Incident settings Create incidents (on by default); group alerts into one incident (up to 150 alerts, 5 hours by default, 5 minutes to 7 days)
Exam tip

. Without entity mappings, the investigation graph cannot be used and alerts cannot be correlated by entity.

3NRT rules

Fact Detail
Schedule Every minute with a one-minute lookback; not configurable
Query A single table; use project to keep results small
Event grouping Per-event alerts are limited to 30 events (29 alerts plus a summary)
Create + Create > NRT query rule

4Threat intelligence and Microsoft security rules

TI map rules match indicators (Module 8) with events, for example TI map IP entity to AzureActivity. Defaults: hourly run, 1-hour lookback, alert when results greater than 0; lookback up to 14 days. Microsoft Threat Intelligence Analytics is a rule that cannot be customized.

A Microsoft security rule turns alerts from other Microsoft security products into incidents automatically. It is not available with Defender XDR incident integration.

5Anomaly rules

Anomaly rules use machine learning to spot unusual behavior and store the results in the Anomalies table.

Step Detail
Built-in rules Cannot be edited
Tune Duplicate the rule, run the duplicate in Flighting mode next to the original in Production mode
Compare Review both results
Promote Switch the duplicate to Production
Exam tip

. Flighting = test. Production = live. Tune an anomaly by duplicating it, not by editing the built-in rule.

6MITRE ATT&CK coverage

Open Microsoft Sentinel > Threat management > MITRE ATT&CK in the Defender portal. The page maps detections to ATT&CK tactics and techniques.

View Meaning
Default Active scheduled and NRT rules
Simulated coverage Detections available but not yet configured, through the Simulated rules menu
View MITRE by threat scenario Filter by threat scenario (Defender portal)

The MITRE ATT&CK workbook and SOC optimization coverage recommendations use the same mapping.

Exam tip

. Gaps in the matrix = missing detections. Simulated shows what you could cover by enabling templates.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A SOC needs an alert within about one minute whenever a break-glass account signs in. The query uses one table. Which rule type fits?

  • AA near-real-time (NRT) rule that runs every minute
  • BA scheduled rule that runs once every 24 hours
  • CAn anomaly rule that runs in Flighting mode only
  • DA threat intelligence rule that matches indicators
Show the answer

Answer: A. NRT rules run every minute on a single table.

S2A scheduled rule returns 30 matching events and creates 30 alerts. The SOC wants one alert per run. Which setting should be used?

  • ASuppression set to 24 hours after each alert is created by the rule
  • BEvent grouping set to group all events into a single alert
  • CAlert threshold set to a minimum of 100 query results
  • DIncident settings set to create no incidents at all
Show the answer

Answer: B. Event grouping controls whether a run produces one alert or one alert per event; one alert per run is the default.

S3An engineer wants to tune a built-in anomaly rule without affecting production detections. What should the engineer do?

  • ADuplicate the rule and run the duplicate in Flighting mode
  • BEdit the built-in rule and switch it to Flighting mode
  • CDelete the built-in rule and import a new custom template
  • DDisable all anomaly rules until the model retrains itself again
Show the answer

Answer: A. Built-in anomaly rules cannot be edited; run a duplicate in Flighting mode, compare, then promote it.

S4After onboarding Sentinel to the Defender portal, an analyst cannot find the Microsoft security incident creation rule type. Why?

  • AThe rule type is available only in the Azure portal after March 2027
  • BThe rule type requires a data lake and is not enabled by default
  • CDefender XDR already creates those incidents, so the rule type is not available
  • DThe rule type is replaced by a Content hub solution that must be installed
Show the answer

Answer: C. Microsoft security incident creation rules (and Fusion) are not available when Defender XDR integration is on.

S5An analyst wants to see which ATT&CK techniques could be covered by detections that exist as templates but are not yet enabled. What should be used?

  • AThe Analytics page with the Active rules tab only
  • BThe MITRE ATT&CK page with the Simulated rules menu
  • CThe Incidents page with a filter on the severity
  • DThe Hunting page with the favorites filter turned on
Show the answer

Answer: B. The MITRE ATT&CK page can show simulated coverage from available but unconfigured detections.

S6A scheduled rule query ends with "search *" to scan every table. What happens when the rule is saved?

  • AThe rule is saved and runs with the data lake
  • BThe rule is saved but runs only once per day
  • CThe query is rejected because search * is not allowed
  • DThe rule is converted to a near-real-time rule
Show the answer

Answer: C. Queries that use search * or union * are not allowed in scheduled rules.

7.2 Recall questions

R1How often does an NRT rule run?

Show the answer

Every minute.

R2What is the range for interval and lookback of a scheduled rule?

Show the answer

5 minutes to 14 days.

R3Which table receives anomaly results?

Show the answer

Anomalies.

R4What is the maximum length of a scheduled rule query?

Show the answer

10,000 characters.

R5Which feature makes the investigation graph work?

Show the answer

Entity mapping.

R6What does Flighting mode do?

Show the answer

Runs a duplicate rule for testing next to the Production rule.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Path Microsoft Sentinel > Configuration > Analytics
Types Scheduled, NRT, TI map, Microsoft security, Anomaly, ML behavior, Fusion
Scheduled 5 minutes to 14 days; 10,000 characters; no search * or union *; simulate last 50 runs
NRT every minute, one table, 30 events per-event grouping
Incidents group up to 150 alerts, 5 hours by default
Anomalies duplicate, Flighting, promote; results in the Anomalies table
MITRE active vs simulated coverage
